increments.title: The context panel gets a working block filter
increments.goal: Give the context panel head a dropdown that lists the block kinds and top-level fields the shown request actually contains, and let the reader hide and show them, against the record the panel already holds.
criteria: The context panel head carries a dropdown built as a `<details>` popover, with no framework and no new dependency, listing every block kind and every top-level field the currently shown request actually contains, one checkbox each, with the number of blocks behind that entry (e.g. `tool_result 12`).

The list is in two labelled groups: **Blocks** first, holding the block kinds present (`assistant`, `other`, `raw`, `system`, `thinking`, `tool_result`, `tool_use`, `user`) sorted alphabetically; then **Fields**, holding the body's remaining top-level keys (`max_tokens`, `metadata`, `model`, `tools`, …) sorted alphabetically. Entries are labelled by the kind name and the field key verbatim, so `system` and `tools` read as one list.
The dropdown holds two buttons, **all on** and **all off**. *All on* makes every entry visible. *All off* hides every entry the currently shown request contains.

Unchecking an entry removes its blocks from the list below; checking it puts them back. Neither triggers a fetch: the filter is applied to the record the panel already holds, and `/api/content/at` is not called again.

The selection is one page-wide state, held as the set of *hidden* entries. It survives a lane change, a scrub, a live refresh and a session change; it is not persisted and a page reload starts with everything visible. An entry never hidden is visible, which is what makes an entry that appears for the first time — a `thinking` block in a later request, a field an earlier body did not carry — arrive visible, including after *all off* was pressed on a request that did not contain it.
An entry the current request does not contain is not listed, and its hidden state is remembered: scrubbing to a request that carries it again shows it still unchecked and its blocks still hidden.

The derivation and the markup are pure functions in `public/context.js` — no `document`, no `fetch`, no `location`, the contract `test/independence.test.mjs` guards — and only the click wiring lives in `app.js`.
The filter's markup carries no `data-lane` attribute and its `<summary>` carries no `data-block`, so opening the dropdown neither toggles the lane selection nor a block's expansion.
An open dropdown survives a repaint: a live refresh that re-renders `#lane-panel` does not snap it shut, the same way `state.expanded` keeps expanded blocks open today.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes after this increment, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
increments.note: Accepted in review round 1: the context panel's filter is built as pure functions in public/context.js with only the click and change wiring in app.js, and the whole suite runs 230 cases at exit 0.

increments.title: The panel head names visible and total, and the empty case says so
increments.goal: Make the filtered panel tell the truth about how much it is hiding: the head names visible-of-total blocks and characters, and a panel with everything hidden shows a placeholder instead of an empty list.
criteria: With nothing hidden, the head line reads as it does today (`210.114 chars · 34 blocks`). With something hidden it names both numbers — visible of total — for blocks and for characters, so the filter can never make a context look smaller than it is. The totals stay readable off `data-chars` and `data-blocks`; the visible counts arrive in data attributes of their own.
With every entry hidden the panel keeps its `data-state="ready"` and shows a placeholder in place of the rows, saying every kind is hidden and where to turn them back on.

The head's new numbers and the placeholder are derived and rendered by pure functions in `public/context.js`, under the contract `test/independence.test.mjs` guards; no new wiring is needed in `app.js` for either.

The cases the previous increment wrote to pin today's behaviour — that a partly filtered panel leaves the head's totals untouched, and that an all-hidden panel renders an empty block list with no placeholder — are updated to the new behaviour in the same change, so no case is left red, skipped or asserting the superseded shape.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes over the whole suite after this increment, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
increments.note: Accepted in review round 1 with no findings: contextCounts is a pure export of public/context.js, the head names visible-of-total chars and blocks with data-visible-chars/data-visible-blocks only while a block is actually hidden, an all-hidden record renders one placeholder in place of the rows with data-state="ready" intact, app.js needed no new wiring, and the whole argus-ui suite ran 238 cases at exit 0.

increments.title: The tools box under the timeline goes, its tick marks stay
increments.goal: Delete the redundant tool list panel and the per-call parameter ballast it forced into page state, while leaving every other tool signal on the timeline exactly as it is.
criteria: `public/tools.js` and `test/tools.test.mjs` are deleted, and `app.js` imports neither `laneToolInput` nor `renderToolPanel`.
`renderLanePanel()` paints only the context panel into `#lane-panel`.

Everything else about tools on the timeline is untouched: the `data-kind="tool"` tick marks on the lane track, the `data-tools` count in each lane's meta, the `tool call` legend entry, and the incremental `/api/events?event=claude_code.tool_result` poll with its `sinceSeq` watermark.

`toolCallOf()` keeps only what a mark needs — `seq`, `timeMs`, `spanId` — and no longer derives or holds `name`, `preview`, `text`, `chars` or `truncated`. `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` and the `paramText()` helper go with it. `mergeToolMarks()` keeps its contract: duplicates dropped by `seq`, the watermark returned as the highest `seq` actually held, the input array untouched.

The context panel comes through the deletion whole: it is still built from one input builder, the filter still renders, hides and reopens, the head still names visible-of-total blocks and characters when something is hidden, and an all-hidden record still shows its placeholder with `data-state="ready"`.

Every case outside the deleted file that asserts the old tool-mark shape or the tool panel's presence — whole-object assertions on `toolCallOf()`'s return among them — is updated or removed in the same change, so no case is left red, skipped or asserting the superseded shape.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes over the whole suite after this increment, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
increments.note: Criterion 5 sharpened after filter-honesty: the panel that must survive this deletion now also carries the visible-of-total head and the all-hidden placeholder, and both ride on the input builder that renderLanePanel feeds, so they are named among what must come through unchanged.

return.summary: Delete public/tools.js and test/tools.test.mjs, strip the tool panel out of renderLanePanel(), and cut toolCallOf() back to seq/timeMs/spanId — leaving the tick marks, the data-tools count, the legend and the incremental tool poll exactly as they are.
return.plan: Delete the tool list panel and the per-call parameter ballast it forced into page state. Six files change; two of them are deleted. ## 1. Delete two files - `tools/argus-ui/public/tools.js` — the whole file (`laneToolInput`, `renderToolPanel`). - `tools/argus-ui/test/tools.test.mjs` — the whole file. ## 2. `tools/argus-ui/public/app.js` - Delete line 18, `import { laneToolInput, renderToolPanel } from './tools.js';`. No other import line changes: `fmtClock`, `resolveCursor`, `mergeToolMarks` and `TOOL_EVENT` all still have callers here. - `renderLanePanel()` (line 948) loses the `+ renderToolPanel(laneToolInput({ … }))` term. The assignment becomes exactly `container.innerHTML = renderContextPanel(lanePanelInput({ view, key: state.selectedLane, held: state.laneContext, expanded: state.expanded, hidden: state.contextHidden, filterOpen: state.contextFilterOpen }));`. Keep `const view = laneView();` and keep passing all six of those fields — `test/page.test.mjs` pins each by name, and `filterOpen`/`hidden` are what increments 1 and 2 built. - Rewrite the `toolMarks` state comment (lines 43-46), which today describes the cap that is going: a mark is now seq, moment and span, and nothing else — enough for the lane's tick marks and its count. - Nothing else in `app.js` reads a mark's `name`, `preview`, `text`, `chars` or `truncated`. The only other consumers of `state.toolMarks` are `buildDensity(…, { tools: state.toolMarks })` at line 208, `mergeToolMarks` at line 903 and the resets at lines 877 and 1063; all keep working unchanged. - Leave the poll at line 895 untouched — `api('/api/events', { session: id, event: TOOL_EVENT, sinceSeq: state.toolSeq, limit: 2000 })` — and leave the `summary[data-block]` expansion wiring alone. The `tool:`-prefixed expansion keys simply stop being produced; `state.expanded` needs no migration, since it is a page-lifetime Set that can no longer gain such a key. ## 3. `tools/argus-ui/public/timeline.js` - Delete `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` (lines 23-24) and the `paramText()` helper (lines 316-327). - `toolCallOf(item)` returns `{ seq: item.seq, timeMs: item.timeMs, spanId: item?.spanId ?? null }` and nothing else. Keep the `?? null` normalisation: `mergeToolMarks`'s cases pin `spanId: null` for an item that carries none. Rewrite its doc comment to say a mark answers *when* a call happened and *whose lane* it belongs to, and that the call's parameters are deliberately not held in page state. - `mergeToolMarks`'s body is untouched. Delete only the sentence in its doc comment that names `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS`. Its contract stands: duplicates dropped by `seq`, the watermark returned as the highest `seq` actually held, non-finite `seq` dropped, the input array copied and never mutated. - Prune `previewOf` from the `./format.js` import on line 15 — line 355 was its only use in this file, so leaving it is a dead import. `esc`, `fmtClock`, `fmtDur` and `fmtNum` all stay. - Reword the `spanLaneKeys` doc comment (lines 83-86), which says the map is "the one the density counts with and the one the tool list is filtered by": the density counts are now its only consumer. - Everything else stays byte-for-byte: `TOOL_EVENT`, `activityMarks`, the `data-kind="tool"` marks on the lane track, `data-tools` in the lane meta, and the legend span at line 521 that reads `tool call`. ## 4. `tools/argus-ui/public/styles.css` Delete the `/* tools */` section — the section header comment plus `.tools-panel`, `.tools-meta`, `.tools-panel .ctx-block > summary` and `.tool-time`, lines ~1235-1256, ending where the `/* events */` header begins. Those four selectors were produced only by `tools.js`; `.ctx-block`, `.ctx-label`, `.ctx-preview` and `.ctx-size` belong to `context.js` and stay. ## 5. Test files that name the deleted things (their edits are spelled out in the test plan) `test/independence.test.mjs` lists `public/tools.js` twice and would go red on the deletion; `test/page.test.mjs` has two cases that only exist for the tool panel and two more that mention it; `test/timeline.test.mjs` pins the old eight-field mark shape in five cases and imports `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` by name (a named import of a removed export is a link-time SyntaxError, so that import must go in the same change). ## Rejected - Keeping `toolCallOf`'s richer shape "in case a later increment wants it": the ballast is the reason this increment exists, and git holds the code. - Leaving the dead CSS behind: a selector no renderer can produce is the same debt in another file. - Purging `tool:` keys out of `state.expanded`: nothing can write one any more, and the Set does not outlive the page. - Touching the `/api/events` poll, the `sinceSeq` watermark, the lane tick marks, the `data-tools` count or the legend: the criteria name each of them as untouched. - The six technical tabs, `DETAIL_VIEWS`, `renderDetailViews()` and everything they drag in: a later increment takes them, so `renderDetailViews` stays imported and called in `app.js` and `fmtNum` stays used by it in `timeline.js`.

return.environment:
Node >= 20.11, already installed. `tools/argus-ui` has zero runtime and zero dev dependencies, so no `npm install` is needed and there is no `node_modules` to create. There is no linter, no formatter and no type checker in this project — nothing to run beyond the tests. The test runner is `node --test` over `test/*.test.mjs`, declared in `tools/argus-ui/package.json`.

Commands, all run from the repository root:

- Whole suite for this project: `npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test`
- One file at a time, while working: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/independence.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs`

No server, no network and no fixture files are needed: every case in these four files is either a pure function call or a `fs.readFileSync` of a file under `public/`.
return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. The suite is `node --test` with `node:assert/strict`; every case is a top-level `test('sentence describing the behaviour', () => { … })`, the sentence written as a statement about the page rather than as a function name, and nearly every assertion carries a message saying what breaking it would cost. Two styles live side by side and must not be mixed: `test/timeline.test.mjs` and `test/context.test.mjs` import the module under test and assert over its return values; `test/page.test.mjs` and `test/independence.test.mjs` read source files with `fs` and assert over their text. Put each case in the file whose style fits it.

## Criterion A — `public/tools.js` and `test/tools.test.mjs` are deleted, and `app.js` imports neither `laneToolInput` nor `renderToolPanel`

**Case A1 (new) — `tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs`, unit, source-level.** Name it after the behaviour, e.g. `test('the tool panel is gone from the page, module and all', …)`. This file already has `const PUBLIC = fileURLToPath(new URL('../public/', import.meta.url));` at line 7; add a sibling `const TEST_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('./', import.meta.url));` beside it or use `new URL('./tools.test.mjs', import.meta.url)` inline. Assert all four:
- `assert.ok(!fs.existsSync(path.join(PUBLIC, 'tools.js')), …)`
- `assert.ok(!fs.existsSync(path.join(TEST_DIR, 'tools.test.mjs')), …)`
- `assert.doesNotMatch(appJs, /from\s*['\"]\.\/tools\.js['\"]/, …)` where `appJs` is read the way every case in this file reads it: `fs.readFileSync(path.join(PUBLIC, 'app.js'), 'utf8')`
- `assert.doesNotMatch(appJs, /\blaneToolInput\b/, …)` and `assert.doesNotMatch(appJs, /\brenderToolPanel\b/, …)`
Place it where the old tool-panel cases were (around line 591), and replace the `// Increment 7 — the click paints the tool list …` section comment with one naming this increment.

**Case A2 (delete) — `tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs` lines 594-600**, `test('app.js takes the tool panel from its module', …)`. It asserts the very import A1 forbids. Delete the whole case.

**Case A3 (edit) — `tools/argus-ui/test/independence.test.mjs`.** Remove the string `'public/tools.js'` from the list at line 33 (`the interface is a project of its own…`) and from the list at line 62 (`nothing in the interface reaches outside the interface`). Both would go red on a file that no longer exists; both must keep every other entry. Nothing else in this file changes — the third case scans only `public/context.js` and `public/timeline.js`.

Run these with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs` and `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/independence.test.mjs`.

## Criterion B — `renderLanePanel()` paints only the context panel into `#lane-panel`

**Case B1 (edit) — `tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs` lines 602-615**, `test('the markup the panels render is what reaches the container', …)`. Rename it to the singular (e.g. `test('the markup the context panel renders is the whole of what reaches the container', …)`), keep the existing `assert.match(renderLanePanel, /container\.innerHTML\s*=\s*renderContextPanel\(/, …)`, delete the `assert.match(renderLanePanel, /\+\s*renderToolPanel\(/, …)` that follows it, and add the "only" assertion: `assert.deepEqual(renderLanePanel.match(/render(?:Context|Tool)Panel\(/g), ['renderContextPanel('], …)`. Use exactly that alternation rather than `render\w*Panel\(`, because `functionSource()` returns the text starting at the declaration and `renderLanePanel(` would match a looser pattern. This is the case that goes red if a second panel is ever concatenated back on.

**Case B2 (delete) — `tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs` lines 617-632**, `test('the tool list is drawn for the selected lane, at the cursor's moment, from the calls the page holds', …)`. Its first assertion calls `callArguments(renderLanePanel, 'renderToolPanel')`, which `assert.fail`s once the call is gone. Delete the whole case.

**Case B3 (edit) — `tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs` lines 494-517**, `test('the panel is drawn from the lane the reader selected and the answer held for it', …)`. Delete the trailing `assert.doesNotMatch(slice, /laneToolInput\(/, …)` (lines 512-516) — it is a tautology once nothing imports that name, and A1 covers it. Keep the `const view = laneView();` assertion but reword its message, which today says "hand the same one to both panels", to say the page builds its lane view once before handing it to the panel. Keep the four `slice` assertions for `view,`, `key:`, `held:` and `expanded:` exactly as they are.

**Already green and must stay green (no edit):** `test('the panel is drawn with the hidden set and the open flag', …)` at line 666 and `test('an open dropdown survives a repaint', …)` at line 712 both read the `renderContextPanel(` argument slice of the trimmed `renderLanePanel`; they are the guard that the trim did not drop `hidden:` or `filterOpen:`.

Run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs`.

## Criterion C — the tick marks, the `data-tools` count, the legend entry and the incremental poll are untouched

**Case C1 (new) — `tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`, unit.** The one signal with no test of its own today is the legend. Add, next to the other `renderTimeline` cases (after line 556 is a good home), `test('the legend still names the tool marks it explains', …)`: build the view the neighbouring case builds — `const content = threeRecordContent(); const view = buildDensity(buildLanes({ session: session(), content }), { content, tools: [toolMark({ spanId: 'sp-a', timeMs: 2200 })] }); const html = renderTimeline(view);` — then `assert.match(html, /<span data-kind="tool">tool call<\/span>/, 'a tick mark nobody can read is not a signal')`. Use the `session()`, `threeRecordContent()` and `toolMark()` fixtures already at the top of the file; add no new fixture.

- `tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs` line 531, `assert.match(row, /data-kind="tool"/, …)` at line 555 — the tick mark on the lane track.

## Criterion D — `toolCallOf()` keeps only `seq`, `timeMs`, `spanId`; `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` and `paramText()` go; `mergeToolMarks()` keeps its contract

All of this lives in `tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`, unit level, module imported directly.

**Import block (edit), lines 4-25.** Remove `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` from the named import — a named import of a removed export is a link-time SyntaxError that takes the whole file down, not one case. Remove `import { previewOf } from '../public/format.js';` at line 25 too; line 607 is its only use and that case is going. Leave every other name in the import list, `DETAIL_VIEWS` and `renderDetailViews` included — the tabs are a later increment.

**Case D1 (replace) — lines 598-612**, today `test('a tool call keeps the tool's name and the parameters it was called with', …)`. Replace it with `test('a tool call is kept as a mark and nothing more, whatever the event carried', …)`: `assert.deepEqual(toolCallOf(toolEvent()), { seq: 5, timeMs: 2200, spanId: 'sp-a' })`. The `toolEvent()` fixture (line 81) carries `tool_name`, `tool_use_id`, `success` and a JSON `tool_input`, so a strict `deepEqual` against three keys is red the moment any of them is derived again. Keep the fixture as it is — an event that carries attributes is exactly what makes this case load-bearing.

**Case D2 (delete) — lines 614-628**, `test('the pre-2.1 attribute name is read when the current one is absent', …)`. Nothing reads `tool_parameters` any more.

**Case D3 (delete) — lines 630-635**, `test('parameters that are not JSON are kept as they arrived, not dropped', …)`. Same reason; this was `paramText()`'s case.

**Case D4 (replace) — lines 637-650**, `test('a call with no parameters and no name is still a row', …)`. Replace with `test('an event with no attributes at all is still a mark, and a missing span becomes null', …)`: `assert.deepEqual(toolCallOf({ seq: 1, timeMs: 1000, spanId: 'sp-a' }), { seq: 1, timeMs: 1000, spanId: 'sp-a' })` and `assert.deepEqual(toolCallOf({ seq: 1, timeMs: 1000 }), { seq: 1, timeMs: 1000, spanId: null })`. The second half is the edge that `mergeToolMarks` depends on.

**Case D5 (replace) — lines 652-666**, today `test('a call whose parameters are a whole file keeps a bounded amount of them, and says how much there was', …)`. Replace with the case that pins the ballast being gone rather than capped: `test('a call whose parameters are a whole file leaves the mark the same size as any other', …)`. Build `const big = 'x'.repeat(50_000); const out = toolCallOf(toolEvent({ attrs: { tool_name: 'Write', tool_input: JSON.stringify({ file_path: '/tmp/big', content: big }) } }));`, then `assert.deepEqual(out, { seq: 5, timeMs: 2200, spanId: 'sp-a' })` and `assert.ok(JSON.stringify(out).length < 200, 'a mark that grows with the call it describes is the megabytes this increment removed')`. Do not reintroduce any character-count constant.

**Case D6 (new) — same file.** `test('the parameter cap is gone from the module, not merely unused', …)`: `import * as timeline from '../public/timeline.js';` at the top of the file (a namespace import beside the existing named one is fine and is the only way to ask about an absent export without a SyntaxError), then `assert.ok(!('TOOL_PARAM_CHARS' in timeline), 'a cap still exported is a cap something can still be capped with')`. `paramText()` was never exported, so its removal is observable only through D1 and D5; that is deliberate and no source scan is added for it — this file is import-only by convention.

**Case D7 (edit) — lines 701-709**, `test('merging into an empty index keeps every call, with the name and parameters a panel draws', …)`. Rename to something like `test('merging into an empty index projects every call through toolCallOf and holds nothing else', …)` and keep the body exactly as it is: the `deepEqual` against `[toolCallOf(…), toolCallOf(…)]` follows the new shape on its own, and its message already says the right thing.

**Case D8 (edit) — lines 774-779**, `test('a missing spanId becomes null rather than undefined', …)`. Change the expected array from the eight-field object to `[{ seq: 3, timeMs: 2000, spanId: null }]`.

**Already green and must stay green (no edit) — the `mergeToolMarks` contract:** lines 711 (a held event is not counted twice), 723 (merging the same response twice is a no-op), 734 (the watermark is what is held), 742 (an item with no usable seq is dropped), 753 (the input array is not mutated), 764 (out-of-order items still leave the highest seq). These six are the whole of "`mergeToolMarks()` keeps its contract"; they need no change and no addition, because the merge's body does not change.

Run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`.

## Criterion E — the context panel comes through the deletion whole

No new case. `tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs` is untouched by this change and already carries a red-on-break case for each half of the criterion; it is the regression net, and the test-author's job here is to confirm it stays green rather than to write anything:
- one input builder — `test('the panel's whole input still comes from one builder', …)`, line 1141
- the filter renders — `test('the dropdown sits in the head, one checkbox per entry, checked, counted, in two labelled groups with two buttons', …)`, line 928
- it hides — `test('unchecking an entry removes its blocks below and only unchecks that box', …)`, line 985
- it reopens across a repaint — `test('the dropdown opens only when asked, and stays open across a repaint', …)`, line 1102
- the head names visible-of-total — `test('a filtered head names the visible numbers beside the totals', …)`, line 1261, with `test('with nothing hidden the head line and its attributes are exactly what they were', …)`, line 1237, as its other half
- all hidden keeps `data-state="ready"` and shows the placeholder — `test('everything hidden shows a placeholder in place of the rows, and a reader can still turn entries back on', …)`, line 1043

Run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/context.test.mjs` if you want it on its own; `npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` covers it.

## Criterion F — every case outside the deleted file asserting the old tool-mark shape or the tool panel's presence is updated or removed

Cases A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, D1-D5, D7 and D8 above are that inventory, exhaustively: they are every hit for `laneToolInput`, `renderToolPanel`, `tools.js`, `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` and the eight-field mark shape outside `test/tools.test.mjs`. No new case guards this criterion; the whole-suite run is its check.

## Left untested, on purpose

- The `styles.css` deletion. There is no CSS test in this project and no renderer can emit `.tools-panel` any more; a test asserting a stylesheet does not contain a string buys nothing.
- The doc-comment rewrites in `timeline.js` and `app.js`. Prose has nothing a tool can check.
- `src/server.mjs` and the collector. Neither is touched.
- Any browser-level rendering of `#lane-panel`. This project has no DOM harness — `page.test.mjs` asserts over source text by design, and that is the level criterion B is provable at.

## What is already red

I ran nothing, and no baseline run is needed to state this. On the production change alone, before the test edits, these go red and are expected to: `test/independence.test.mjs` (both lists name `public/tools.js`), `test/timeline.test.mjs` (fails to load at all — it imports `TOOL_PARAM_CHARS` by name), and the four `page.test.mjs` cases named in A2, B1, B2 and B3. Every one of them is addressed above; after the edits the whole suite must be green in one run.

increments.title: The six technical tabs go out of the code
increments.goal: Remove the pre-timeline tab interface — its views, its state, its wiring and its per-refresh fetches — and land the whole issue with both suites green.
criteria: `DETAIL_VIEWS` and `renderDetailViews()` are gone from `public/timeline.js`, and no tab nav is rendered anywhere.

Gone from `public/app.js`: `renderTabBody()`, `renderOverviewTab()`, `renderTodosTab()`, `renderTracesTab()`, `renderWaterfall()`, `renderSpanInspector()`, `renderEventsTab()`, `renderMetricsTab()`, `renderRawTab()`, `loadTabData()`, the helpers only they used (`kpi`, `formatValue`, `spanKind`, `spanNote`, `todoStatusChip`, `SPAN_KINDS`), the `#tab-body` container, and the state fields `tab`, `trace`, `selectedTraceId`, `selectedSpanId`, `events`, `eventFilters`, `metrics`, `facets`.

Gone from the wiring in `wireEvents()`: the handlers for `[data-tab]`, `[data-trace]`, `[data-span]` and `[data-event-seq]`, the `change` handler for `event-filter` and `event-errors`, and the `event-search` branch of the `input` handler. The 15-second interval no longer repaints a tab body.
`renderDetail()` no longer builds the `counts` object, and no refresh requests `/api/traces`, `/api/facets` or `/api/metrics`. The `/api/events` request that feeds the tool marks stays.
No unused import or dead helper is left behind in `app.js` or `timeline.js`, and the tests that pinned the removed views are removed with them rather than left skipped.

The `change` and `input` listeners the context filter and the rest of the page still need survive the removal: the filter's checkboxes, the *all on* and *all off* buttons and the lane selection all still work.
`src/server.mjs` is unchanged: it proxies `/api/*` blindly and knows no route by name.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` is green over the whole suite, and each criterion above has at least one test that goes red when its behaviour is broken or removed.
`./test.sh` is green.

increments.title: The context panel gets a working block filter
increments.goal: Give the context panel head a dropdown that lists the block kinds and top-level fields the shown request actually contains, and let the reader hide and show them, against the record the panel already holds.
criteria: The context panel head carries a dropdown built as a `<details>` popover, with no framework and no new dependency, listing every block kind and every top-level field the currently shown request actually contains, one checkbox each, with the number of blocks behind that entry (e.g. `tool_result 12`).

The list is in two labelled groups: **Blocks** first, holding the block kinds present, sorted alphabetically; then **Fields**, holding the body's remaining top-level keys, sorted alphabetically, labelled verbatim.
The dropdown holds two buttons, **all on** and **all off**.
Unchecking an entry removes its blocks from the list below and checking it puts them back, with no new fetch of `/api/content/at`.
The selection is one page-wide set of hidden entries, surviving lane change, scrub, live refresh and session change, not persisted, with anything never hidden arriving visible.
An entry the current request does not contain is not listed, and its hidden state is remembered.
The derivation and the markup are pure functions in `public/context.js`, and only the click wiring lives in `app.js`.
The filter's markup carries no `data-lane` and its `<summary>` no `data-block`.
An open dropdown survives a repaint.
`npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` passes, with a red-on-break test per criterion.
increments.note: Accepted in review round 1: the filter is pure functions in public/context.js with only click and change wiring in app.js, suite 230 cases exit 0.

return.summary: filter-honesty was accepted with no findings and is closed done: contextCounts landed as a pure export of public/context.js, the head names visible-of-total chars and blocks only while a block is actually hidden, an all-hidden record renders one placeholder with data-state="ready", app.js was untouched, and the suite ran 238 cases at exit 0. The re-cut is deliberately small — the two open increments are removals whose scope this increment did not disturb. One criterion changed: tools-box's 'the context panel comes through unchanged' now names the visible-of-total head and the all-hidden placeholder among what must survive, because both are new since that criterion was written and both hang off the same input builder renderLanePanel feeds when the tool panel is torn out of it. I left tabs-out untouched: its criterion that the shared change and input listeners survive already covers the filter wiring, and nothing filter-honesty showed touches the tab code. I considered and rejected two re-cuts. Merging tools-box and tabs-out into one removal increment: they delete different things for different reasons, each leaves the repository working alone, and one review over both would be a 600-line diff plus a module deletion. Splitting tabs-out into views-and-state then wiring-and-fetches: removing a render function without its handler leaves a dead listener and a half-migrated file, so it is one change, and the budget (6 of 8 increments left for 2) does not force a split. One thing worth a reader's eye but not a criterion: contextCounts shipped with two call shapes, the documented object form plus an optional second positional argument, because the test author and the plan disagreed on the signature; the review accepted it, and narrowing it is not in this issue's criteria, so I did not invent an increment for it.
